title: National pride can remain strong while everyday cohesion and institutional legitimacy weaken
source_unit: AthenaLab, National Identity and Social Cohesion: Chile in Perspective
geography: Chile; nationally representative adult survey fielded 30 July-16 August 2025 across 70 municipalities, plus qualitative interviews and grounded-theory analysis

observations.period: August 2025; interpersonal trust and institutional trust

denominator.unit: Chilean adults aged 18+ surveyed by CATI in 70 municipalities covering approximately 70% of the national population

interpersonal_carefulness.unit: percent saying one must be very careful when dealing with people

most_people_trusted.unit: percent saying most people can be trusted

police_trust.unit: percent reporting a lot or quite a bit of trust in police

armed_forces_trust.unit: percent reporting a lot or quite a bit of trust in the armed forces

congress_low_trust.unit: percent reporting little or no trust in Congress

party_low_trust.unit: percent reporting little or no trust in political parties

institutional_asymmetry.value: Trust is higher in order-and-security institutions than in representative political institutions

observations.method: Descriptive weighted CATI survey of 1,000 adults, weighted by sex and age using Chilean statistical projections; the study also includes qualitative research that is not representative.
observations.uncertainty: Trust is self-reported and institution-specific; the survey is concentrated in municipalities covering about 70% of the population and does not establish causal sources of distrust.
observations.subgroup: Chilean adults, with institution-specific comparisons across police, armed forces, municipalities, executive, courts, Congress, and parties.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher trust in security institutions may reflect different expectations or salience rather than a generalized preference for coercive authority over democracy.

observations.period: August 2025; national pride, division, and identity-state separation

denominator.unit: Chilean adults in the national survey

very_proud.unit: percent rating pride in being Chilean at the maximum level

more_divided.unit: percent saying Chilean society is more divided than ten years ago

high_polarisation.unit: percent saying there is a high level of political polarisation

identity_elements.unit: percent naming culture, traditions, and customs among the two most representative elements of Chilean identity

belonging_legitimacy_gap.value: National identity retains emotional strength while the institutions organizing political life are viewed as weak or distant

observations.method: National survey with closed-ended measures of pride, perceived division, polarization, and identity content, supplemented by qualitative interpretation.
observations.uncertainty: The measures show coexistence, not a causal relationship between pride and institutional distrust; identity answers are sensitive to wording and current political context.
observations.subgroup: Chilean adults across political, territorial, and generational positions.
observations.counterinterpretation: High pride may itself be a form of political or cultural positioning, and perceived division may reflect heightened attention rather than greater interpersonal conflict.

observations.period: August 2025; territorial identity and migration perceptions

denominator.unit: Chilean adults in the national survey

regional_identity_distinct.unit: percent saying their regional identity differs from national identity

immigration_weakened_identity.unit: percent saying foreign arrivals have weakened national identity

immigration_strengthened_identity.unit: percent saying foreign arrivals have strengthened national identity

attitude_to_foreigners_divided.unit: percent describing Chilean society as divided between inclusion and rejection of foreigners

migration_identity_mechanism.value: Migration simultaneously pressures an older national imaginary and creates a route toward plural identity, with everyday acceptance and public threat narratives coexisting

observations.method: Survey questions on regional identity, immigration and perceived effects on national identity, interpreted alongside qualitative interviews on everyday versus political reception.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived immigration effects are not measures of actual migration impacts, service use, crime, labor competition, or integration outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Residents identifying with regions and the nation; perceptions of Venezuelan, Haitian, Colombian, and other recent migration.
observations.counterinterpretation: Migration may be a proxy for broader insecurity, institutional failure, or political messaging rather than the direct cause of identity concern.

observations.period: Qualitative study; crisis and everyday cohesion mechanisms

denominator.unit: Qualitative interview and grounded-theory material; participant count and sampling frame are not stated in the extracted publication section

episodic_cohesion.value: Solidarity intensifies during earthquakes, fires, sporting victories, mass celebrations, and named humanitarian causes, then fades in ordinary life

face_and_name.value: Concrete, personalized narratives activate cooperation more readily than abstract structural problems

everyday_fragility.value: Reactive unity does not automatically become durable social capital or continuous cooperation

institutionalisation_route.value: Civic education, inclusive migration policy, decentralization, and institutional reform are proposed as bridges from symbolic solidarity to everyday cohesion

observations.method: Qualitative interviews and grounded-theory axial coding across categories including positive cultural traits, reactive unity, threats to cohesion, migration dynamics, and historical evolution.
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative findings provide mechanisms and interpretations, not population prevalence or causal effect sizes; participant selection and coding procedures limit generalization.
observations.subgroup: Interview participants describing family, territory, crisis solidarity, migration, political conflict, and institutional trust.
observations.counterinterpretation: Episodic solidarity may be a normal complement to everyday institutions rather than evidence that cohesion is structurally fragile.

related_sources.claim: AthenaLab study landing page describing theoretical, qualitative, interview, and national-survey components.
AthenaLab event summary reporting headline findings and study context.

boundary: This record adds a nation-state cohesion mechanism: emotional national belonging can persist while interpersonal trust, representative-institution legitimacy, and everyday cooperation weaken; migration and crisis solidarity expose the boundary. It does not establish causal effects, actual integration outcomes, violence, service burden, or generalize beyond the Chilean study design.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official English AthenaLab PDF reviewed for methodology, survey denominator, trust measures, pride, division, polarization, regional identity, immigration perceptions, qualitative mechanisms, and study boundaries.
